subject: Request: Short-term consumption subsidy for MedNova pilot
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@mednova.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot usage spike — short-term subsidy request

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the MedNova team is excited to move into a small, 8-week pilot to validate inference quality on their private VPC. We've started ingesting telemetry and have attached the first-week consumption snapshot (mednova_usage_report_q1.csv).

Quick context: their initial test runs show bursts that would exceed the committed-monthly throughput by ~3.5x for short windows while they validate integration. This is expected to normalize after the second month, but the overage exposure is large enough that Procurement is asking for a short-term consumption subsidy to bridge the proof-of-value period.

Ask: Can Redwood provide a 90-day temporary subsidy that covers up to 60% of incremental overage tokens for the pilot period? MedNova proposes a stacked rebate: 40% immediately applied to overage invoices for month 1, then 20% reduction month 2, and removal month 3. They are willing to commit to a 12-month contract if pilot metrics are met.

We need confirmation on whether this qualifies as a pricing exception requiring VP/CFO approval. Can you advise next steps and what financial data you need?

Thanks,
Olivia Grant
Head of Platform Partnerships
MedNova Therapeutics
attachments: mednova_usage_report_q1.csv (CSV, 34KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot usage spike — short-term subsidy request

Folks — forwarding MedNova's request. Key points: 8-week pilot, front-loaded burst that creates ~3.5x overage risk in month 1, customer asks for a temporary 90-day tapering subsidy (40/20/0). They will do an annual commitment if pilot passes.

Requesting: 1) A short pricing exception memo we can route to Finance (Laura) for sign-off; 2) An estimated revenue impact and recommended guardrails (rollback, metric gates).

Jonas, can you draft a one-pager we can send to Finance? Marissa, FYI on commercial terms and rollback. Lauren, any engineering gating we should require on the pilot (rate limits, KV cache locks)?

Thanks — I want to respond to Olivia by EOD with next steps.

Irene
Director, Global Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Pilot usage spike — short-term subsidy request

Irene / team —

Draft memo for Finance below. High-level recommendation is to approve a time-bound, usage-tiered subsidy with strict metric gates and an early termination clawback if the annual commitment isn't executed. Estimated 90-day P&L impact if fully drawn: ~$28k gross margin reduction (assuming blended unit economics from MedNova's usage profile).

--- PRICING EXCEPTION MEMO (draft) ---
Customer: MedNova Therapeutics (Deal: DN-19832)
Request: 90-day consumption subsidy to reduce overage exposure during an 8-week pilot. Proposed taper: Month1=40% subsidy on incremental overage, Month2=20%, Month3=0%.
Rationale: Pilot is technical validation on private VPC; high burst is expected and temporary. Customer committed to 12-month annual contract contingent on pilot pass.
Financial impact: Estimated max realized subsidy (if customer draws full burst): $28,000 (gross margin impact). Realistic draw estimate: ~$12-15k.
Conditions & guardrails:
- Subsidy capped at $30k total.
- Customer must sign MOP v2 (attached) with obligation to convert to annual plan within 45 days of pilot completion or repay a prorated portion of subsidy.
- Auto-disable: subsidy ends after 90 days or at contract conversion, whichever comes first.
- Technical gating: limit sustained RPS via rate-limiter and enable KV cache warmup to reduce peak token generation. Lauren to confirm feasibility and toggle plan.
Next steps: Finance approval (Laura). On approval, Sales to send formal offer and DocuSign MOP v2.
--- end memo ---

Attachments: proposed_mop_v2.pdf (term sheet)

If approved, recommend we mark this as a one-time exception and record in the pricing exceptions tracker. Marissa — I added the $30k cap; we can tighten if Finance prefers.

Jonas
VP, Commercial Growth
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Pilot usage spike — short-term subsidy request

Laura — adding context for Finance review:
- Commercial ask is explicitly tied to accelerated conversion risk. If MedNova converts, subsidy is fully commercialized in renewed rate card and we recover via committed ARR.
- Suggested controls: subsidy cap ($30k), conversion window (45 days), and a repay clawback if customer doesn't convert.
- Billing ops impact: need a one-off credit schedule and marking the invoices as 'pilot subsidy' for audit.

I've attached the current draft MOP and put the conversion language in section 3. Can Finance review and confirm whether the $30k cap and 45-day conversion condition are acceptable. Also confirm whether VP or CFO signature is required for this level — my read is CFO signoff.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through numbers.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Pilot usage spike — short-term subsidy request

Team — reviewed Jonas' memo and estimated impact. Approve the one-time subsidy with the following binding conditions:
1) Cap at $25,000 (revised down from $30k)
2) Signed MOP v2 executed and lodged in DocuSign prior to subsidy effective date.
3) 30-45 day conversion window: if no signed annual conversion by day 45, the customer repays a prorated portion of subsidy (see clause 3.4 in MOP v2).
4) Finance will require subsidy accounting code "PILOT_SUBSIDY_2027" for audit trail and will schedule a follow-up review 60 days after subsidy start.

Irene/Jonas: please update memo reflecting the cap change and route the term sheet to customer with the required clauses. Once DocuSign is signed, Billing will apply the subsidy credit.

Approved by,

Laura Bennett
CFO, Redwood Inference
attachments: none
